content.title: About
content.content: Popcorn cake is a dessert made of layers of airy popcorn soaked in a sweet syrup and covered with cream or glaze. Nuts, dried fruits or chocolate crumbs are often added, giving it a crunchy and aromatic character.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Popcorn cake originated in the United States in the early 2000s as a novel alternative to traditional cakes.
A special "popcorn mousse" is used to keep the crunch even after syrup soaking.
The cake can be adapted for dietary restrictions, using gluten‑free syrup and plant‑based creams.
It is a popular choice for kids' parties and street‑food festivals.
There is a "milk" version where popcorn is coated with caramel sauce and milk chocolate.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Air‑popped popcorn contains little fat, making the cake potentially less caloric than traditional butter‑rich cakes.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Popcorn is rich in dietary fiber, which supports healthy digestion.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Polysaccharides and polyphenols in popcorn have antioxidant properties.

items.title: Gluten‑free (when prepared with appropriate ingredients)
items.content: Using gluten‑free syrup and cream makes the cake suitable for people with celiac disease.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Popcorn provides small amounts of B1 and B3 vitamins, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to corn, making popcorn cake unsuitable for them.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: The syrup and glaze often contain a lot of sugar; people with diabetes should limit portions.

items.title: Dental hazard
items.content: Crunchy popcorn pieces can get stuck between teeth, especially in children.

items.title: Caloric load with add‑ins
items.content: Adding nuts, chocolate, or buttercream significantly increases the calorie count.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the cake into serving pieces and serve at room temperature. It pairs well with berry sauce, ice cream, or fresh fruit. For a lighter option, choose versions without chocolate crumbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the popcorn cake in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a tightly sealed bag – up to 2 months. Before serving, let the cake come to room temperature so the cream softens.
